14 A car of mass 1100 kg is travelling at a constant speed of 15 m s–1 up a slope inclined at 10° to the
horizontal. The combined frictional forces acting on the car are directed down the slope and are
W , where W is the weight of the car.
equal to 5
15 m s–1
10°
What is the useful output power of the car’s engine?
A
28 kW
B
32 kW
C
60 kW
D
190 kW

hints: Notice the car moves at constant $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$ up the $10^{\circ}$ slope, so the forward driving force must exactly balance both downhill forces: the $W\sin10^{\circ}$ component of weight and the $W/5$ friction.
Recall useful power for motion at speed $v$ against a force $F$ along the direction of motion is $P=Fv$, so you need the total resistive force up the slope before multiplying by $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate $W=mg$ for $1100\text{ kg}$, then add $W\sin10^{\circ}$ to $W/5$ to get about $4030\text{ N}$, then multiply by $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and convert to $\text{kW}$.
walkthrough: Find the weight: $W = mg = 1100 \times 9.81 \approx 10790\text{ N}$. This acts vertically downwards.
Resolve downhill along the $10^{\circ}$ slope. The component is $W\sin10^{\circ} \approx 10790 \times 0.1736 \approx 1870\text{ N}$ down the slope.

Add the frictional force down the slope: $F_{f} = W/5 \approx 10790/5 \approx 2160\text{ N}$. At constant speed resultant force is zero, so engine driving force $F = W\sin10^{\circ} + W/5 \approx 1870 + 2160 \approx 4030\text{ N}$ up the slope.
Use $P = Fv$ for force parallel to velocity: $P = 4030 \times 15 \approx 60500\text{ W} \approx 60\text{ kW}$.

A.explanation: This is only the power to overcome the $W\sin10^{\circ}$ component of weight, about $28\text{ kW}$, and omits the $W/5$ frictional force down the slope.

B.explanation: This is only the power to overcome friction, $(W/5)v$ about $32\text{ kW}$, and omits the component of weight down the $10^{\circ}$ slope.

C.explanation: The driving force balances $W\sin10^{\circ}+W/5$ and $P=Fv$ gives about $4030 \times 15 \approx 60\text{ kW}$.

D.explanation: This uses the full weight $W$ plus friction, $(W+W/5)v \approx 190\text{ kW}$, instead of only the $W\sin10^{\circ}$ component down the slope.
